questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Interesting human rights-oriented electives at the host university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My overall experience at Universidade Catolica Portuguesa was very good. I had some interesting electives, met exchange students from all of the world, and the campus of the university was nice.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The information provided by the host university was very limited upon arrival as the plan of electives and courses was not final before the beginning of the semester. It meant that I could not fill out the OLA, have my electives accepted at Københavns Universitet upon arrival and apply for my Erasmus Grant before the start of the semester.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The host university held a welcome session for all exchange students at the beginning of the semester. At the welcome session we finally got all the information about courses that we needed to apply for our Erasmus grant.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is difficult to find cheap housing in the city centre of Lisbon but there are several Facebook housing groups, but I actually ended up finding something on airbnb.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you want to live in a nice, central area of Lisbon, you need to start searching well in advance in order to find cheap housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We got an email from the international office of the host university with information and a guide to register. It was easy to follow.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was possible to write an email to the international office of the host university, and if they knew the answer, they would reply really quick. Unfortunately, information about the available courses came very late, so they were not able to provide much information about that upon arrival.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted to have.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is easy, and if you have any question, the international office at the university is very helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were many different seminars and courses. However, many of them were small seminars of 3-4 ECTS points, so it meant that I had to choose 7-8 seminars in order to get 30 ECTS points. Therefore, I almost had all the electives available at the university.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was different from course to course depending on the teacher.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. The level of participation was very important for one's final grade, and most of the exams were handwritten exams of 2 hours.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: EU Asylum and Migration Law, International Criminal Law, The Law of the WTO, We the Peoples - the UN as a Legal Forum, The Law of Fighting Poverty, Introduction to International Legal Theory, Introduction to Global Law, Right to Fair Trial.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend The Law of the WTO and We the Peoples - the UN as a Legal Forum. The Law of WTO is taught by a guest teacher from New York University (NYU), and he is very inspiring and made the topic surprisingly interesting. The teacher of We the Peoples - the UN as a Legal Forum is a member of the ILC and head of the legal department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Portugal, and she both has a deep academic knowledge of the topic and a practical view on the functioning of the UN.

questions.answer: I did not hear of any clubs or sports activities on campus.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not hear about any available on campus.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go surfing, go on trips outside of Lisbon (Sintra, Caparica, Cascais), and visit some of all the good museums in Lisbon.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy, and I like really like the Portuguese culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The most challenging part was that many things are decided last minute. For example, the semester plan was final the first week of the semester, and I was supposed to get the courses accepted at KU in advance.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Portuguese people are very social, they meet outside at night, eat well and in the whole month of June, there is a huge street festival in Lisbon with community dining, barbecuing and music.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: You will get most information when the semester has already started but things will be sorted out eventually.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The host university provides "seminars" and "courses". "Seminars" are electives with classes of 1-2 weeks ending with the final exam during the semester, while "courses" have 1-2 classes every week all semester with the final exam in the exam period, around a month after the last week of classes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting all the other exchange students from all of the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: In some weeks, I had 3-4 seminars at the same time which meant that I had classes from 08:00-20:00 at the university, ending with 4 exams in only 2 days.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
